input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds us (Customer) with a post-term non-compete of twenty-four months, covering any product or service that "competes with Vendor" in any territory. That is walk-away territory on two counts: a post-term restriction longer than 12 months, and undefined scope with no field, product or territory limits and no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (indeed "acquire" is expressly prohibited). It therefore fails the fallback, which would permit only a named competing product, during the term, capped at 12 months, with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs. It also flatly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete... commitment." Preferred position is no restriction at all, so we delete § 12.4; § 12.3 already covers the point, and we offer the narrowed fallback in the comment if Vendor identifies a specific product needing protection.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept any restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted § 12.4; it also directly contradicts § 12.3, which confirms we have made no non-compete commitment. If you need protection for a specific product, we can discuss a narrow restriction limited to a named competing product during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month, all-territory non-compete binding Customer in § 12.4.
